Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY forms.mjs render.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json TRUST_PROXY=false
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# Form Inbox

After using this, you can now **point any HTML form at your own server and get an inbox, spam filtering and notifications**, instead of paying a form service a monthly fee that grows with your submissions and sending your visitors' messages through it.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/form-inbox/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: paste a submission and see its spam score and the reasons. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: one Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file. Form endpoints, an admin inbox, CSV export and notifications.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Form Inbox |
|---|---|---|
| Formspree, Basin, Getform, Web3Forms | Hosted; metered per month; spam tools and exports on higher tiers; messages live with them | Your server, unlimited forms, all included |
| Netlify Forms and other host features | Tied to one host | Any static host; one endpoint URL |
| A homemade mail script | You secure and maintain it; no inbox, review or export | Tested, escaped, rate limited, with an admin inbox |

Honest limits: no file uploads, autoresponder is a fixed text, one admin key (no per-user logins), and heuristic spam scoring, not a trained model.

## Use it

```html
<form action="https://your-server/f/<form id>" method="post">
  <input name="name"> <input name="email" type="email"> <textarea name="message"></textarea>
  <input name="_gotcha" tabindex="-1" autocomplete="off" style="position:absolute;left:-9999px" aria-hidden="true">
  <button>Send</button>
</form>
```

Create forms at `/admin` (any user name, `ADMIN_KEY` as the password). JSON works too: `POST /f/<id>` with `Content-Type: application/json`. Fields starting with `_` are control fields and are not stored: `_gotcha` is the honeypot, and `_ts` (milliseconds since epoch when the page loaded) lets the server penalise instant submissions.

Per form you can set **allowed sites** (browsers on other sites are refused), a **thank-you URL** (only ever the one you configured, so it cannot be used as an open redirect) an **email address** for notifications, and an optional **auto-reply** text. The auto-reply goes only to the address in the visitor's email field, only for submissions that are not spam, at most once a day per address and form, and contains only the text you wrote (nothing the visitor typed), so the endpoint cannot be used to mail strangers. It needs email configured and follows `DRY_RUN`.

## Spam scoring

Score 0 to 100, spam at 50 or more. Signals: filled honeypot (decisive), submitted under 2 s after load, more than 2 / 5 links, spam phrases, mostly capitals, malformed or disposable email, identical to a submission in the last hour, empty. Flagged entries go to the Spam tab with their reasons, never notify, and the sender still sees a normal success. Mark any entry spam or not spam by hand. Posts are limited to 10 a minute per address per form; addresses are held in memory only and never written to disk.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/form-inbox
node --test        # no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs
```

API: `GET /admin/f/<id>.csv` (spreadsheet-formula-safe CSV export, same key as `Authorization: Bearer ...`).

Optional: `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack/Discord, https) pings on each real submission; `RESEND_API_KEY` + `MAIL_FROM` email the address set on a form, starting in dry-run (`DRY_RUN=false` turns real email on). Other settings: `STATE` (JSON file path; keep it on a persistent disk), `PORT`, `PUBLIC_URL`, `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind a proxy, `HIDE_SPONSOR_LINK=true`, `RETENTION_DAYS` (delete submissions older than this many days, checked hourly; default keeps them). The newest 5,000 submissions are kept.

## One-click deploy

Fork the repository, then open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. Render builds the Dockerfile in **your** account with a 1 GB disk and generates `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's accounts. The same Dockerfile runs on Fly.io, Railway or any VPS. Serve it over HTTPS only (Render does); the admin uses HTTP Basic auth.

## Disclaimer

No warranty; no uptime or delivery guarantee. You operate the forms and are responsible for the messages collected, your privacy notice and data-protection rules. The spam score can be wrong either way. Not legal, tax or financial advice. MIT licensed. If it saves you a subscription, you can [sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

## Other self-deploy paths

`docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker (the command is at its top). Fly.io: the steps are at the top of `fly.toml`. Both keep state on a volume and run in your own account.

docker-compose.yml.text:
# Any box with Docker:
#   ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)  docker compose up -d
# Put it behind HTTPS (Caddy, nginx, a tunnel) before real use.
services:
  form-inbox:
    build: .
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    volumes: ["state:/data"]
    environment:
      ADMIN_KEY: ${ADMIN_KEY:?set ADMIN_KEY}
      STATE: /data/state.json
      TRUST_PROXY: ${TRUST_PROXY:-false}
      COMPANY_NAME: ${COMPANY_NAME:-}
      ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL: ${ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL:-}
volumes:
  state:

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "form-inbox-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
Your contact form, your server, no per-submission fee.

Form Inbox is the open-source backend for the forms on your static site. Point a form's action at it and you get an inbox, spam filtering that shows its reasons, CSV export and email or Slack notifications. Below, test the spam filter on a message. Everything on this page runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.

Try the spam filter

 

 

    The server uses this exact scoring. At 50 or more a submission goes to the Spam tab, nothing is sent, and the sender still sees a normal thank-you.

    Why someone would use this

    TodayCatchForm Inbox
    Formspree, Basin, Getform, Web3FormsSubmissions are metered per month; spam tools, exports or integrations sit on higher tiers; your visitors' messages live with themYour server, unlimited forms, everything included
    Netlify Forms and similar host featuresTied to one host; spam and volume limits come with the planWorks with any static host, one endpoint URL
    Your own mail script (PHP, serverless function)You write, secure and maintain it; no inbox, spam review or exportTested, escaped, rate limited, with an admin inbox

    Honest limits: no file uploads, no autoresponder to the visitor, no multi-user logins (one admin key), and heuristic spam scoring rather than a trained model: expect to mark a few entries by hand.

    Run it yourself

    git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/fp-monorepo && cd fp-monorepo/ventures/form-inbox
node --test
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs

    Open http://localhost:8080/admin (any user name, ADMIN_KEY as the password), create a form, and paste its snippet into your site. One-click Render deploy and Docker are in the README.

    Questions

    Why not just use Formspree, Basin, Getform or Netlify Forms?

    Those hosted services are polished and the right call if you want zero setup. They meter submissions per month, put spam filtering, file storage or exports on higher tiers, and keep your visitors' messages on their servers. Form Inbox is one small Node server in your own account: unlimited forms and submissions within your disk, spam scoring, CSV export and notifications included. If a free hosted plan already covers your volume, keep it.

    How does the spam filter work?

    Each submission gets a score from 0 to 100 from transparent signals: a hidden field bots fill in, a form submitted within two seconds of loading, link floods, common spam phrases, disposable email domains, and repeats of a recent submission. At 50 or more it goes to the Spam tab, no notification is sent, and the sender still sees a normal success page so bots learn nothing. Every flagged entry shows its reasons, and you can mark any entry as spam or not spam.

    Can anyone post to my form from any website?

    Only if you leave Allowed sites empty. Set it to your site's origin and browsers on other sites are refused; requests with no Origin header (curl, servers) are still accepted, so the rate limit and spam score do the rest. Posts are limited to ten a minute per address per form.

    Where do notifications go?

    Real submissions can ping a Slack or Discord webhook and email the address set on the form through your own Resend account. Email starts in dry-run mode and sends nothing until you set DRY_RUN=false. Spam never notifies.

    What does it store?

    The fields people submit, a timestamp and the spam score. No IP addresses are written to disk; they are held in memory only to rate limit. Delete a submission or a whole form from the admin page. You are the operator of any form you run and responsible for your privacy notice.

    Same builder, other jobs: Feedback Board collects feature requests, Status Keeper runs a public status page, MRR Pulse shows MRR and churn and Webhook Relay forwards webhooks reliably.

    No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator of any form you run, responsible for the messages it collects, a privacy notice, data-protection rules where you and your visitors live, and your own email sending. The spam score is a heuristic and can be wrong either way. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

    Sponsor on GitHub ·

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# No third-party key is required. ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL (Slack/Discord) and Resend email are optional.
services:
  - type: web
    name: form-inbox
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/form-inbox
    dockerfilePath: ventures/form-inbox/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
        sync: false
